It involves three parts: **The server** sends the `X-XSS-Protection` header to block cross-site scripting; **The browser** validates it and ignores these headers; then the browser checks the `X-Frame-Options`, `Content-Security-Policy`, and referrer field values; finally, only certain websites are allowed to submit data back.  
For instance, if the domain name used in the `Referer` is different from the original page’s URL before the link was clicked, the browser treats it like a new request, thus sending back its own information instead of the one the attacker intended.  
In other words, if the victim visited <http://www.site1.com> first, clicked on <https://sited2/some/other/url/page.html>, but went directly back to <https://site3/com/> after submitting the same form twice, the third-party's JavaScript would automatically send two requests to their servers.
